  (5) If the head of a Si/Gun/Gu fails to notify a person who has filed a report of whether to accept such report or of the extension of the processing period thereof under statutes and regulations concerning the processing of civil petitions, within the relevant period specified in paragraph (4), the report shall be deemed accepted on the day following the end of the period (referring to the extended or re-extended period if the processing period is extended or re-extended under the statutes and regulations concerning the processing of civil petitions). <Added on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (6) Where a report filed under paragraph (1) is accepted (including cases in which a report is deemed to have been accepted pursuant to paragraph (5)), a transferee, or a surviving or resulting corporation following merger or consolidation shall succeed to the status of the previous construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater on the date such take over or merger takes place. <Added on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (7) Where a report filed under paragraph (2) is accepted, the successor shall succeed to the status of construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater, and the registration of the construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater filed for the decedent during the period between the date of the decedent's death to the date of receipt of the report shall be deemed registration for the successor. <Added on Jan. 5, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 25 (Revocation of registration) (1) Where a construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater falls under any of the following cases, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may revoke his or her registration; provided, where he or she falls under any of subparagraphs 1, 4, 5 and 7, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall revoke his or her registration: <Amended on Dec. 27, 2016>
  1. Where he or she has registered his or her business under Article 22 (1) by improper means;
  2. Where he or she ceases to meet the criteria for registration under Article 22 (1);
  3. Where he or she fails to register changes under Article 22 (1) or registers changes by improper means;
  4. Where he or she falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 23; provided, this shall not apply to cases where a corporation any of whose executive officer falls under any of subparagraphs 1 through 5 of Article 23 replaces such executive officer within three months;
  5. Where he or she allows another person to conduct construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater by using his or her trade name or name, or lends a certificate of registration, in violation of Article 26;
  6. Where he or she fails to conduct business for at least two consecutive years;
  7. Where he or she performs faulty construction works on facilities for the development and utilization of groundwater by intent or gross negligence;
  8. Where the State or a local government requests the revocation of registration pursuant to the related statutes, such as the National Tax Collection Act or the Local Tax Collection Act.
  (2) A construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater, who is subject to the revocation of registration pursuant to paragraph (1), may continue to perform the construction works which he or she commenced before such cancellation, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Matters necessary for procedures, etc. for the revocation of registration under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 26 (Prohibition of name lending) No construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater shall allow another person to conduct construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater by using his or her trade name or name, or lend his or her registration certificate to another person.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 26-2 (Establishment of trade association) (1) Enterprises and experts related to the development and utilization of groundwater may establish an association (hereinafter referred to as the "Association") for the development of technology and institutional improvement related to the development and utilization of groundwater and for the sound development of the industry.
  (2) The Association shall be a juristic person.
  (3) In order to establish the Association, the industry related to the development and utilization of groundwater and 10 or more related experts shall promote the Association and prepare the articles of association at the inaugural general meeting, and file an application for authorization with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) When the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment authorizes an application under paragraph (3), he or she shall publicly announce the authorization thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) The Association shall conduct the following affairs: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Investigation and research on the development and utilization of groundwater;
  2. Technical development and education on the development and utilization of groundwater and the preservation of water quality;
  3. Publication of various published materials concerning the development and utilization of groundwater;
  4. Affairs entrusted by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment;
  5. Public relations with the people for the preservation and management of groundwater, and inspiration of awareness for environmental protection;
  6. Other activities necessary to achieve the purposes of the establishment of the Association.
  (6) Matters necessary for the articles of incorporation of the Association, and guidance and supervision of the Association shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (7) Except for matters provided for in this Act, the provisions on incorporated associations of the Civil Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Association.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

CHAPTER V GROUNDWATER IMPACT INVESTIGATION AGENCY

Article 27 (Registration of groundwater impact investigation agency) (1) A person who intends to conduct affairs of groundwater impact investigation required to apply for permission under Article 7 or 13 shall register such affairs with the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the seat of his or her main office, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. The same shall also apply to cases where he or she intends to change matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as his or her trade name or name, among the registered matters.
  (2) Matters necessary for the criteria and procedures for registration under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 28 (Grounds for disqualification of groundwater impact investigation agency) None of the following persons shall file an application for registration under Article 27 (1): <Amended on Apr. 18, 2017>
  1. A person who falls under any of subparagraphs 1 through 4 of Article 23;
  2. A person in whose case two years have not passed since the registration of a groundwater impact investigation agency was revoked pursuant to Article 29 (1) (excluding the cases where the registration was revoked as he or she falls under the subparagraph 1 or 2 of Article 23);
  3. A juristic person any of whose executive officer falls under any of subparagraph 1 or 2.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 29 (Cancellation of registration of groundwater impact investigation agency) (1) Where a person who files for registration under Article 27 (1) (hereinafter referred to as "groundwater impact investigation agency") falls under any of the following cases, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may cancel the registration of a groundwater impact investigation agency; provided, where the groundwater impact investigation agency falls under subparagraph 1, 4, 5 or 7, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall cancel its registration:
  1. Where it has registered by improper means;
  2. Where it fails to file for registration of changes under Article 27 (1) or registration of changes by improper means;
  3. Where it ceases to meet the criteria for registration under Article 27 (2);
  4. Where it falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 28; provided, this shall not apply to cases where a corporation any of whose executive officer falls under any of subparagraph 1 or 2 of Article 28 and such executive officer is replaced within three months;
  5. Where it allows another person to conduct a groundwater impact investigation by using his or her trade name or name or lends a certificate of registration to another person, in violation of Article 30;
  6. Where it subcontracts all the affairs of groundwater impact investigation;
  7. Where it conducts a poor groundwater impact investigation by intent or gross negligence.
  (2) Matters necessary for procedures, etc. for the cancellation of registration under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 29-2 (Registration of groundwater purification business) (1) A person who intends to engage in groundwater purification business shall have capital, technological capacity, facilities, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree and register his or her business with the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the seat of his or her main office. The same shall also apply to cases where he or she intends to change matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as his or her trade name or name, among the registered matters.
  (2) Only a person who has registered groundwater purification business may engage in groundwater purification business; provided, this shall not apply to insignificant purification works prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Article 23 through 26 shall apply mutatis mutandis to groundwater purification business. In such cases, "construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater" shall be construed as "groundwater purification business," and "construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater" shall be construed as "groundwater purification contractor".
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 30 (Prohibition of name lending) No groundwater impact investigation agency shall allow another person to conduct a groundwater impact investigation by using its trade name or name, or lend its registration certificate to another person.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

CHAPTER V-2 SECURING AND MANAGEMENT OF REVENUE SOURCES

Article 30-2 (Establishment of special account for groundwater management) (1) A Si (including a Special Self-Governing City; hereinafter the same shall apply)/Gun/autonomous Gu may establish a special account for the management of groundwater (hereinafter referred to as "special account") in order to raise funds, etc. required for the proper development and utilization and preservation and management of groundwater and the quality control of drinking water within its jurisdiction. <Amended on May 22, 2013; Dec. 31, 2024>
  (2) The special account shall be created by the following revenue sources: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. Subsidies from a Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City or Do;
  2. Charges for using groundwater and additional charges under Article 30-3 (1) 1;
  2-2. Charges for using groundwater and additional charges paid in accordance with Article 30-3 (8) among charges for using groundwater and additional charges under paragraph (1) 2 of that Article; provided, in cases of a Special Self-Governing City, it shall be an amount equivalent to 2/3 of the charges for using groundwater and additional charges under paragraph (1) 2 of that Article;
  3. Money transferred from the general account and other special accounts;
  4. Loans;
  5. Gains generated from the management of funds referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 4;
  6. Deposits of performance guarantees under paragraph (3);
  7. Administrative fines under Articles 39 and 40.
  (3) Where performance guarantees deposited pursuant to Article 14 are cash, they shall be deposited in the special account.
  (4) The special account shall be used for the following purposes: <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. Surveys on groundwater and surveys on the actual conditions of the use of groundwater under Article 5;
  2. Formulation and execution of regional management plans;
  3. Management of groundwater preservation zones;
  4. Restoration under Article 15;
  5. Purification works for polluted groundwater under Article 16-3;
  6. Installation and operation of ancillary measurement networks under Article 17;
  7. Redemption of loans under paragraph (2) 4;
  8. Repayment of deposits of performance guarantees under paragraph (3);
  9. Making up fees for water quality testing under Article 33 (2);
  10. Promotion of drinking water quality management policies under Article 5 (1) of the Drinking Water Management Act;
  11. Other projects for the purposes prescribed by Presidential Decree, which are necessary for the preservation and management of groundwater and the quality control of drinking water.
  (5) Matters necessary for the compilation of the budget, settlement of accounts and management of the special account shall be prescribed by municipal ordinance of a Si/Gun/autonomous Gu.
  (6) Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu formulates a plan for the use of the special accounts every year or modifies such plan he or she has formulated (excluding modification of insignificant matters prescribed by Presidential Decree), he or she shall report such plan or modified plan to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Mayor/Do Governor, as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor shall report such plan or modified plan to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment only. <Amended on May 22, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 30-3 (Imposition and collection of charges for using groundwater) (1) The Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may impose and collect charges for using groundwater according to the following classifications in order to raise revenue sources necessary for the proper development, utilization, preservation, and management of groundwater and the quality control of drinking water: <Added on Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. Where charges for using groundwater are imposed on and collected from a person who develops and utilizes groundwater after obtaining permission in accordance with Article 7 or filing a report in accordance with Article 8: The head of a Si/Gun/Gu;
  2. Where charges for using groundwater are imposed on and collected from a person who has obtained permission to develop spring water or saline groundwater (hereinafter referred to as "spring water, etc.") in accordance with Article 9 of the Drinking Water Management Act, a person who has obtained permission to manufacture drinking spring water or drinking saline groundwater (hereinafter referred to as "drinking spring water, etc.") in accordance with Article 21 (1) of that Act, and a person who has registered import-sale business of drinking spring water, etc. in accordance with paragraph (3) of that Article: The Mayor/Do Governor.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may reduce or exempt charges for using groundwater (limited to charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1)) in any of the following cases: <Amended on Jun. 22, 2015; Dec. 8, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. Cases falling under Article 8 (1) 1, 3 and 4;
  2. Where groundwater is developed and utilized for the purpose of farming under subparagraph 1 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Agriculture, Rural Community and Food Industry and fishery business under subparagraph 1 (a) of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Fisheries and Fishing Villages Development and aquaculture business under item (e) of that subparagraph;
  3. Where groundwater is developed and utilized, aiming at engaging in general water supply business under subparagraph 19 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act;
  4. Where a fee for using river water is imposed in accordance with Article 50 (7) of the River Act;
  5. Where groundwater is developed and utilized for purposes and on a scale prescribed by Presidential Decree, other than the cases referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 4.
  (3) Charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1) shall be the amount classified as follows: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. Charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1) 1: The amount prescribed by municipal ordinance of a Si/Gun/autonomous Gu within the limits of 50/100 of the amount equivalent to charges for using water under Article 19 of the Act on the Improvement of Water Quality and Support for Residents of the Han River Basin, in consideration of volume of groundwater collection, purposes, etc.;
  2. Charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1) 2: The amount prescribed by Presidential Decree not exceeding 3 times the total sum of the following amounts calculated on the basis of water intake volume for persons who have obtained permission to develop spring water, etc. in accordance with Article 9 of the Drinking Water Management Act and persons who have obtained permission for business of manufacturing drinking spring water, etc. under Article 21 (1) of that Act and on the basis of import volume of drinking spring water, etc. for persons who have registered import-sale business of drinking spring water, etc. under Article 21 (3) of that Act:
    (a) Costs of tap water and costs of sewerage under Article 21 of the Local Public Enterprises Act;
    (b) Charges borne by causers under Article 71 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act;
    (c) Charges on burden-causing entities under Article 61 of the Sewerage Act;
    (d) The average of the following water use charges:
  1) Water use charges under Article 19 (1) of the Act on the Improvement of Water Quality and Support for Residents of the Han River Basin;
  2) Water use charges under Article 32 (1) of the Act on Water Management and Residents Support in the Nakdong River Basin;
  3) Water use charges under Article 30 (1) of the Act on Water Management and Resident Support in the Geum River Basin;
  4) Water use charges under Article 30 (1) of the Act on Water Management and Resident Support in the Yeongsan and Seomjin River Basins;
    (e) Expenditure in the category of waterworks and water quality conservation of the national environmental improvement projects under Article 47 (1) 1 of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy.
  (4) A person who has obtained permission to develop spring water, etc. in accordance with Article 9 of the Drinking Water Management Act shall install and maintain measuring instruments capable of measuring intake water volume, and submit the results of measurement to the Mayor/Do Governor, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Added on Dec. 31, 2024; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) Matters necessary for the detailed methods of calculation, imposition and collection, and procedures for payment of charges for using groundwater under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be determined in accordance with the following classifications: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. Charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1) 1: Municipal ordinance of a Si/Gun/autonomous Gu;
  2. Charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1) 2: Presidential Decree.
  (6) Where a person liable to pay charges for using groundwater in accordance with paragraph (1) fails to pay the charges for using groundwater by the deadline for payment, the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall collect additional charges prescribed by Presidential Decree within the limit not exceeding 3/100 of the charges for using groundwater in arrears for the period from the day following the deadline for payment to the day before the payment date. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2024>
  (7) Where a person who is liable to pay charges for using groundwater under paragraph (1) or additional charges under paragraph (6) fails to pay such charges by the deadline for payment, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall collect the charges in accordance with the Act on the Collection of Local Administrative Penalty Charges. <Amended on May 22, 2013; Aug. 6, 2013; Mar. 24, 2020; Dec. 31, 2024>
  (8) The Mayor/Do Governor shall disburse an amount equivalent to 2/3 of the charges for using groundwater and additional charges collected from persons prescribed by Presidential Decree, among persons who have obtained permission to develop spring water, etc. and permission to manufacture drinking spring water, etc. in accordance with paragraphs (1) 2 and (6), to a Si (excluding a Special Self-Governing City), Gun, or autonomous Gu where the relevant spring is located. <Added on Dec. 31, 2024>
  (9) Charges for using groundwater imposed and collected in accordance with paragraph (1) shall be used for the purposes prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 30-2 (4). <Added on Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2024>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 30-4 (Special cases concerning filing objections to charges for using groundwater) (1) Where a person who has been imposed with charges for using groundwater has an objection to the imposed charges for using groundwater, he or she may file an objection within 30 days from the date he or she is imposed on the charges for using groundwater.
  (2) Upon receipt of an objection filed under paragraph (1), the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall deliberate on the objection within 15 days from the date of receipt of the objection and notify the applicant of the result thereof in writing.
  (3) Matters necessary for the methods of filing an objection, deliberation, notification of the results thereof, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), Article 36 of the Framework Act on Administration (excluding the proviso of paragraph (2) of that Article) shall apply to matters concerning filing objections.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2024]

Article 30-5 (Deferment of collection or installment payment of charges for using groundwater) (1) Where a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu deems that a person liable to pay charges for using groundwater is unable to pay the charges for using groundwater due to any of the following grounds before the deadline for payment of the charges for using groundwater, he or she may defer the collection thereof or allow him or her to pay the charges in installments:
  3. Where it is deemed inevitable to defer the payment of such charges or to pay them in installments on the grounds, etc. corresponding to those referred to in subparagraphs 1 and 2.
  2. Where he or she is in a serious business management crisis after suffering a business loss;
  3. Where it is deemed inevitable to defer the payment of such charges or to pay them in installments on the grounds, etc. corresponding to those referred to in subparagraphs 1 and 2.
  (2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu defers the payment of charges in accordance with to paragraph (1), he or she may ask the person liable to pay such charges to provide security equivalent to the amount deferred.
  (3) Where the person liable to pay charges falls under any of the following cases, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may revoke the deferment of payment of the charges under paragraph (1) and collect the charges in arrears in a lump sum. In such cases, the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall notify the person liable to pay the charges of the fact in advance:
  1. Where he or she fails to pay the charges in arrears by the specified deadline;
  2. Where he or she refuses to comply with a just request of the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu to replenish the security, including an exchange of such security;
  3. Where the deferment is deemed no longer necessary on the grounds of a favorable change in his or her property situation or other changes in circumstances.
  (4) Matters necessary for the period of deferment of collection of charges, the frequency of the payments in installments, methods of filing an application for the deferment of collection under paragraph (1), and other matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2024]

CHAPTER VI SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 31 (Access to land of others) (1) When it is necessary for investigation, purification, or measurement under Article 5, 7 (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 13 (3)), 16-4, or 17 the head of the relevant administrative agency, an institution specialized in surveys of groundwater, a groundwater impact investigation agency, or a groundwater purification contractor may have access to land of others or may temporarily use land of others, and, if specially necessary, may alter or remove bamboos and trees, earth and rocks, or other obstacles. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) Where an institution specialized in surveys of groundwater, a groundwater impact investigation agency, or a groundwater purification contractor intends to have access to land of others pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall obtain permission from the head of a Si/Gun/Gu and notify the owner, occupant, or manager of the relevant land of the date and time and place of such access not later than three days before it intends to have access to such land.
  (3) Where the head of the relevant administrative agency, an institution specialized in surveys of groundwater, a groundwater impact investigation agency, or a groundwater purification contractor intends to temporarily use land of others or to alter or remove bamboos and trees, earth and rocks, or other obstacles pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall obtain consent from the owner, occupant, or manager of the relevant land; provided, where it cannot obtain consent from the owner, occupant or manager of land or obstacles because he or she is not at the spot or his or her domicile or residence is unclear, it may temporarily use land of others or may alter or remove obstacles by obtaining permission from the head of a Si/Gun/Gu.
  (4) No person shall have access to land of others, enclosed by a wall or fence, without consent from the occupant of land before sunrise and after sunset.
  (5) A person who intends to perform an act under paragraph (1) shall produce an identification card indicating his or her authority or permit card to the relevant persons.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 32 (Compensation for loss) (1) Where a person who performs an act under Article 31 (1) inflicts losses on another person due to having access to land, temporary use of land, or alteration or removal of obstacles, he or she shall give due compensation to the person who suffers losses.
  (2) A person who is to give compensation for loss and another person who suffers losses shall agree on compensation for loss under paragraph (1).
  (3) Where both parties fail to come to an agreement under paragraph (2) or cannot reach an agreement, the relevant parties may apply for decision to the competent Land Expropriation Committee.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 33 (Fees) (1) A person who intends to file an application for permission, testing, or registration falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall pay fees to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu (in cases of subparagraph 3, referring to an institution specialized in testing related to groundwater under Article 20 (1)), as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Permission for the development and utilization of groundwater under Article 7 (1) or permission for changes under Article 7 (6);
  2. Permission for the development and utilization of groundwater under Article 13 (1) 1;
  3. Water quality testing under Article 20 (1);
  4. Registration of construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater or registration for changes under Article 22 (1);
  5. Registration of a groundwater impact investigation agency or registration of changes under Article 27 (1);
  6. Registration of groundwater purification business or registration of changes under Article 29-2.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), in any of the following cases, fees under the said paragraph may be reduced or exempted; provided, fees referred to in paragraph (1) 3 may be reduced or exempted, as prescribed by ordinance of a local government, however, the relevant local government shall make up the difference of expenses for water quality testing due to the reduction of or exemption from fees to an institution specialized in testing related to groundwater by utilizing the special account for the management of groundwater under Article 30-2: <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  1. Where a person who intends to apply for permission, testing or registration referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) is the State or a local government;
  2. Where a person who intends to apply for testing referred to in paragraph (1) 3 uses groundwater as drinking water in his or her daily life for home use in an area where tap water is not supplied.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 34 (Reporting and inspection) (1) When it is required to ascertain whether requirements for registration and statutes or regulations are violated, or a civil complaint, etc. is filed, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may have a construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater, a groundwater impact investigation agency or a groundwater purification contractor submit necessary data or file a report within a fixed period not exceeding one month.
  (2) Where it is impracticable to achieve the purpose of inspection according to the result of the examination of the content of submitted data and a report under paragraph (1), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may have the relevant public officials have access to the relevant place of business to inspect the relevant matters.
  (3) When the head of a Si/Gun/Gu conducts an inspection under paragraph (2), he or she shall advise a person subject to inspection of a plan for inspection including the date and time of, reasons for and the content of such inspection not later than seven days before he or she conducts the inspection; provided, this shall not apply in cases of emergencies or to cases where he or she deems that he or she cannot achieve the purpose of inspection due to the destruction of evidence, etc. if he or she advises in advance.
  (4) A public official who conducts an inspection pursuant to paragraph (2) shall produce an identification card indicating his or her authority to the relevant persons, and when he or she has access to a place of business, he or she shall deliver a document stating his or her name, the time and the purpose of having access to the place of business, etc. to the relevant persons.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 34-2 (Education) (1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may formulate and promote policies on education and training of engineers when necessary for the efficient utilization and improvement of technical capability of technological human resources related to the development and utilization of groundwater. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Workers and engineers in the business related to the development and utilization of groundwater shall receive education and training conducted by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, and matters necessary for those subject to education, the content of education, educational institutions, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may entrust affairs of education and training under paragraphs (1) and (2) to an institution or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 34-3 (Reporting on business results) (1) Any of the following persons shall report business results, the status of technical capabilities, facilities, and equipment he or she has, the training completion status of engineers, etc. to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu every 2 years, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. A person who files for registration of a construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater under Article 22 (1);
  2. A person who files for registration of a groundwater impact investigation agency under Article 27 (1);
  3. A person who files for registration of a groundwater purification business under Article 29-2 (1).
  (2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall compile the data submitted in accordance with paragraph (1) and report such data to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Mayor/Do Governor; provided, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor shall only report to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Added on Jan. 5, 2021]

Article 35 (Hearings) Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu intends to make any of the following dispositions, he or she shall hold a hearing:
  1. Revocation of permission for the development and utilization of groundwater under Article 10 (1) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 13 (3));
  2. Cancellation of registration of construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater under Article 25 (1) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 29-2 (3));
  3. Cancellation of registration of a groundwater impact investigation agency under Article 29 (1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 36 (Delegation of authority) (1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may partially delegate his or her authority under this Act to the heads of affiliated agencies or a Mayor/Do Governor, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 8, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) A Mayor/Do Governor may partially delegate his or her authority under this Act to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 36-2 (Vicarious execution) Where a person who is ordered to close facilities under Articles 8 (4) and 9 (3) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in accordance with Article 13 (3)), to restore facilities or land to the original state under Article 15 (3), to prevent the pollution of groundwater under Article 16 (2) or (3), or to perform purification works under Article 16-3 (1) and (2) fails to comply with such order, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may perform vicarious execution, as prescribed by the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act and collect the relevant expenses from the person who has violated the order. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

CHAPTER VII PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 37 (Penalty provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for at least three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won: <Amended on Jan. 6, 2015; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. A person who develops and utilizes groundwater without obtaining permission under Article 7 (1) or with permission obtained by improper means;
  2. A person who performs any of the following acts referred to in Article 13 (1) without obtaining permission under Article 13 (1) or with permission obtained by improper means;
  3. A person who violates an order to prevent the pollution of groundwater under Article 16 (2);
  3-2. A person who fails to comply with an order to suspend the operation and use, or to close down, dismantle, or remove facilities causing groundwater pollution under Article 16 (3);
  4. A person who fails to comply with an order to purify groundwater pollutants under Article 16-3 (1), or to suspend the operation and use, or to close down, dismantle or remove facilities causing groundwater pollution under Article 16-3 (2);
  5. A person who engages in construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater, affairs of groundwater impact investigation, or groundwater purification business, without filing for registration under Article 22 (1), 27 (1) or 29-2 (1) or after filing for registration by improper means;
  6. A construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater who constructs facilities for the development and utilization of groundwater without obtaining permission, approval, etc., in violation of Article 22 (3).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 37-2 (Penalty provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for at least two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won: <Amended on Jan. 6, 2015>
  1. A groundwater impact investigation agency that prepares a false groundwater impact inspection report under Article 7 (2);
  2. A person who fails to take measures for preventing groundwater pollution under Article 16 (1);
  3. A person who fails to take measures for preventing pollution, to install an observation well, or to measure water quality under Article 16-2 (1);
  4. A person who fails to file a report on the occurrence of pollution, or to take measures for preventing pollution under Article 16-2 (2).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 37-3 (Penalty provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for at least 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won: <Amended on Jan. 6, 2015; Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2024;>
  1. A person who fails to observe the limits of the collection volume of groundwater under Article 7 (3);
  2. A person who develops and utilizes groundwater without obtaining permission for changes under Article 7 (6) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 13 (3)) or after obtaining permission for changes by improper means;
  3. A person who fails to observe the limits of the volume and period of water collection, or to comply with an order to take a corrective action, an order to suspend the utilization of groundwater, an order to jointly utilize groundwater, or an order to close down facilities under Article 8 (4);
  4. A person who fails to comply with an order to close down facilities under Article 9 (3) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 13 (3));
  5. A person who fails to formulate or implement a plan for using groundwater runoff under Article 9-2 (2) or to comply with an order to make improvements under paragraph (4) of that Article;
  5-2. A person who fails to take necessary measures under Article 9-2 (10);
  6. A person who fails to comply with an order to improve facilities or fails to take necessary measures under Article 9-4 (4);
  7. A person who performs purification works without obtaining approval of a purification plan or approval for changes under Article 16-4 (1);
  8. A person who engages in construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater, groundwater impact investigation, or groundwater purification business without filing for registration of changes under Article 22 (1), 27 (1) or 29-2 (1) or after filing for registration of changes by improper means;
  9. A construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater who violates Article 26 (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 29-2 (3)), a groundwater impact investigation agency that violates Article 30, or the other party to whom a groundwater purification contractor lends his or her name or lends his or her certificate of registration.
  10. A person who fails to install measuring instruments under Article 30-3 (4) or a person who fails to submit measurement results or submits false measurement results.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 38 (Joint penalty provisions) If the representative of a corporation, or an agent or employee of, or any other person employed by, a corporation or an individual commits an offense referred to in Article 37, 37-2 or 37-3 in connection with the business affairs of the said corporation or individual, not only shall such offender be punished, but also the juristic person or individual shall also be punished by a fine referred to in the relevant Article; provided, this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not negligent in giving due attention and supervision concerning the relevant affairs in order to prevent such offense.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

Article 38-2 Deleted. <Jan. 16, 2001>

Article 39 (Administrative fines) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 5 million won: <Amended on Jan. 23, 2024>
  1. A person who fails to file a report on the development and utilization of groundwater or files a false report, in violation of Article 8 (1);
  2. A person who excavates land without filing a report on excavation, in violation of the former part, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 9-4 (1);
  3. A person who fails to implement necessary measures, such as an order issued by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu to take a corrective action or the suspension of utilization under Article 9-5 (4);
  4. A person who fails to restore facilities or land, in violation of Article 15 (1), or fails to comply with an order to restore facilities or land, in violation of paragraph (2) or (3) of that Article;
  5. A manager of facilities causing groundwater pollution who fails to report the result of water quality measurement under Article 16-2 (1) or files a false report;
  6. A person who fails to comply with orders to take measures, such as the suspension of the utilization of groundwater or water quality improvement, under Article 20 (2);
  7. A person who refuses, interferes with, or evades an inspection under Article 21 (3) or 34 (2);
  8. A construction contractor for the development and utilization of groundwater, who constructs facilities for the development and utilization of groundwater without filing a report, in violation of Article 22 (3).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 5, 2021]

Article 40 (Administrative fines) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 3 million won: <Amended on Jan. 23, 2024>
  1. A person who fails to report changes or files a false report on changes, in violation of Article 8 (2);
  2. A person who fails to file a report on completion of construction, in violation of Article 9 (1) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 13 (3));
  3. A person who fails to report the status of groundwater runoff, in violation of Article 9-2 (1);
  4. A person who fails to report a plan for using groundwater runoff or a plan for the modification thereof, or to report the completion of use of groundwater runoff, in violation of Article 9-2 (2);
  5. A person who fails to report the completion of the development and utilization of groundwater, in violation of Article 9-3 (1);
  6. A person who fails to report a change or completion, in violation of the latter part, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 9-4 (1);
  7. A person who fails to report succession or files a false report, in violation of Article 11 (1) or (2);
  8. A person who fails to deposit a performance guarantee, in violation of Article 14 (1);
  9. A person who fails to undergo water quality testing, in violation of Article 20 (1);
  10. A person who fails to file a report or submit data under Article 21 (1) or (2), or 34 (1), or files a false report or submits false data;
  11. A person who fails to report succession to construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater or groundwater purification business under Article 24 (1) or (2) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 29-2 (3)), or files a false report;
  12. A person who refuses, interferes with, or evades access, etc. under Article 31 (1);
  13. A person who performs an act under Article 31 (1) without obtaining permission or giving advance notification, in violation of Article 31 (2);
  14. A person who engages in an activity under Article 31 (1) without obtaining consent or permission from the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, in violation of Article 31 (3).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 5, 2021]

Article 40-2 (Administrative fines) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 300 thousand won:
  1. A person who files a false report on completion of the implementation of follow-up management, in violation of the latter part of Article 9-5 (2);
  2. A person who fails to keep the results of water quality testing under Article 20 (4).
  [This Article Added on Jan. 5, 2021]

Article 41 (Procedures for imposition and collection of administrative fines) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall impose and collect administrative fines under Articles 39, 40, and 40-2, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

ADDENDA <Act No. 17850, Jan. 5, 2021>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force 1 year after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Applicability to reporting plans for using groundwater runoff)
The amended provisions of Article 9-2 (2) shall begin to apply where the construction of a ground floor is completed after this Act enters into force.
Article 3 (Applicability to reporting on excavation)
The amended provisions of Article 9-4 (1) shall begin to apply to the excavation of land for developing and using groundwater after this Act enters into force.
Article 4 (Applicability to reporting on succession to rights of persons who develop and utilize groundwater)
The amended provisions of Article 11 (3), and 24 (4) and (5) shall begin to apply where a report on succession to rights and obligations of a person who develops or utilizes groundwater or a report on the transfer or merger of a construction business for the development and utilization of groundwater is filed after this Act enters into force.
Article 5 (Applicability to imposing charges for using groundwater)
The amended provision of Article 30-3 (1) shall begin to apply to the imposition of charges for using groundwater after this Act enters into force.
Article 6 (Transitional measures concerning orders to improve measures for reduction of groundwater runoff)
Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu issues an order for improvement for a failure to take measures for the reduction of groundwater runoff under previous Article 9-2 (3) as at the time this Act enters into force, the previous provisions shall apply.
Article 7 (Transitional measures concerning orders to prevent pollution of groundwater)
Where the Minister of Environment or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu issues an order to prevent the pollution of groundwater pursuant to previous Article 16 (2) at the time this Act enters into force, the amended provisions of Article 16 (3) shall apply.
Article 8 (Transitional measures concerning penalty provisions or administrative fines)
The application of penalty provisions or imposition of administrative fines for offenses committed before this Act enters into force shall be governed by the previous provisions.
Article 9 Omitted.
